overview: This Senate resolution honors the life of Alan K. Simpson, who represented Wyoming in the U.S. Senate from 1979 to 1997. It recounts his Army service, his law career, and his years in the Wyoming legislature, and notes that he served as a Senate party whip and chaired the Senate Veterans' Affairs Committee. It highlights his focus on immigration, veterans, and the national debt, his role co-chairing a 2010 national commission on federal finances, and his 2022 Presidential Medal of Freedom. The resolution expresses the Senate's sorrow, sends a copy to his family, and adjourns the Senate in his memory. The Senate agreed to it and sent word to the House on March 31, 2025.
for: Supporters say it is a fitting tribute to a senator known for his public service, his work on veterans and fiscal issues, and his humor.
against: Critics say it is a symbolic gesture that does not change any law or spending.
